titolo: Jensen Huang: 'I'd Be Honored' to Return. Nvidia Says No.
angolo: Day 3: the board pushes back on the FT's comeback report via Reuters and CNBC sources, while Trump says it is not a bad idea and Kress faces her first earnings call.
descrizione: Jensen Huang Wants Nvidia Back. The Board Says No. The Financial Times reports Huang has discussed a comeback; Reuters and CNBC, citing sources, say Nvidia's board is not considering it. Trump says it "certainly isn't a bad idea," and interim CEO Colette Kress faces her first earnings call on Tuesday. Here is what is confirmed, what is only reported, and what happens next.

scene.testo: Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back, three people told Reuters.
Yet days after he left, the Financial Times reports he is weighing a comeback, citing people familiar with the matter.
Nvidia has lost roughly 500 billion dollars in market value since the scandal broke, according to CBC and other outlets.
Can a founder who resigned amid a scandal really walk back into his own company?
First, what is confirmed. Nvidia announced on November 12 that Huang resigned as CEO, effective immediately.
CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. Harvey Jones became the board's first-ever chair.
The board said it would search for a permanent CEO, internal and external candidates alike.
What is not confirmed: any decision to bring Huang back. Nvidia has not announced one.

visivo.testo: Reported is not the same as confirmed

scene.testo: Spokespeople for Nvidia and for Huang declined to comment to the Financial Times.
But that is only the start of this story.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it as CEO for 33 years.
He took Nvidia from a startup to a world leader in accelerated computing, according to the company's filing.
In December 2025, the Financial Times named him its Person of the Year.
Huang holds about a 3.6 percent stake in Nvidia, according to Yahoo Finance.
He led the company for 33 years. Then, in days, it unraveled.
Nvidia's board launched an investigation after reports that Huang had been targeted by a Chinese espionage operation.
Huang acknowledged being unfaithful. Reports allege the affair was with Alice Huang, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Fact check: those are reports and U.S. intelligence suspicions reported by the New York Times, not a court finding.
The New York Times also reported that Huang had an affair with a subordinate, Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.
Nvidia's board announced Thursday morning that Huang had resigned.
Nvidia shares closed down about 4.3 percent on the day he resigned, after plunging earlier.
Analysts across a number of banks cut their price targets on Nvidia after Huang's ouster.
Then came the weekend, and a very different story.
On Sunday, the Financial Times reported Huang is considering a comeback, citing people familiar with the matter.
One ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return.
The same ally said the effort had Huang's support, and that they would try to garner support from the White House.
"Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen."

citazione.testo: Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen

scene.testo: That is the unnamed ally's claim, as reported by the FT and relayed by Reuters.
Two shareholders, Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides's Gavin Baker, wrote an open letter to the board on Friday.
They urged directors to keep all options on the table, including a Huang return.
The letter did not demand immediate reinstatement, and said the board has the prerogative to decide otherwise.
An online petition has drawn nearly 180,000 signatures, CNBC reported. Reuters counted more than 180,200.
Elon Musk has backed the petition, and he is listed among its signatories.
Other signatories include Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator's Garry Tan is also backing the campaign.
But the board has a different message.
The Nvidia board is not considering bringing Jensen back, three people familiar told Reuters.
That is according to three people who spoke to Reuters. Nvidia has not said this on the record.
CNBC reported the same Monday, citing a person familiar with the matter.
The board is reportedly focused on its investigation of Huang's conduct, not his return.
Nvidia hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead that probe.
It will examine whether national security or company secrets were compromised.
On Friday, a board representative said only that it was selecting a search firm.
The FT also reported that the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor.
Arm is a British chip design company. Nvidia has not publicly confirmed the approach.
But the board is not the only power in this story.
On Monday, President Trump said of a Huang return: "That certainly isn't a bad idea."
He also said he "would certainly not mind seeing that," per LBC.
"I think he learned a big lesson."

citazione.testo: I think he learned a big lesson

scene.testo: Asked about reports that Alice Huang was a suspected Chinese asset, Trump said, "I don't know that she is a spy."
The Washington Post reported Trump's trades this year suggest he held between 13 and 62 million dollars of Nvidia stock as of the end of August.

grafica.sotto: Washington Post: Trump's Nvidia stock, August

scene.testo: Meanwhile Congress is waiting. House panels are seeking Huang's testimony on December 1.
Trump left Monday on a trip to Asia, including China, where he is expected to meet President Xi Jinping.
There is one more place where Huang's fall is felt.
Taiwan, where Huang was born, and where he enjoys a celebrity-like status called Jensanity.
Investors, though, are more divided.
One institutional investor, speaking anonymously, told Reuters they would be wary of Huang returning, noting that Apple and Microsoft thrived after their visionary CEOs left.
Independent researcher Richard Windsor told Reuters that shareholders would ultimately be better served by his return.
T Rowe Price analysts said a transition may call for a new structure rather than just a new executive.
Now the first real test arrives. Tuesday, after the bell, Nvidia reports third-quarter earnings.
Analysts expect revenue of about 109.1 billion dollars, up 91 percent, per CNBC and LSEG.
This time, interim CEO Colette Kress leads the call and is expected to face questions on the leadership search.
CNBC says she is likely to be pressed on China sales, neocloud exposure and the company's leadership.
Kress has said she is committed to "building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years."

citazione.testo: I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years

scene.testo: Analyst Dan Ives, per Newsweek, rejects a Huang return despite the shareholder push.
So what do we actually know? Huang resigned, Kress is interim CEO, and a search for a permanent CEO is underway.
The FT reports he is weighing a return. Reuters and CNBC sources say the board is not considering it.
House panels are seeking Huang on December 1. The board's outside investigation by Wachtell Lipton is still running, per CNBC.
Follow this story, because it is still developing.
